chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Musa ibn Sa'dan, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from al-Hasan ibn Rashid, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام) saying: "Indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, when He loves to create the Imam, He commands an angel. So he takes a drink from water beneath the Throne and gives it to his father to drink. From that the Imam is created. Then he remains for forty days and nights in the womb of his mother, not hearing sound; then after that he hears speech."

So when he is born, that angel is sent and writes between his eyes: "And the Word of your Lord has been completed in truth and justice; there is none who can alter His words, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing."

Then when the Imam who was before him passes away, a beacon of light is raised for this one by which he looks upon the deeds of the creatures. By this Allah establishes the proof against His creation.

key_terms.أَعْمَالِ الْخَلَائِقِ: the deeds of created beings, which the Imam is said to behold
key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: the Imam, the divinely appointed leader spoken of in the narration
key_terms.الْعَرْشِ: the Throne, mentioned as the place beneath which the water is taken
key_terms.شَرْبَةً: a drink or draught taken from the water beneath the Throne
key_terms.كَلِمَةُ رَبِّكَ: the Word of your Lord, cited in the Quranic phrase written upon him
key_terms.مَلَكًا: an angel commanded by Allah to carry out this matter
key_terms.مَنَارٌ مِنْ نُورٍ: a beacon of light raised for the Imam after the previous Imam passes
key_terms.يَحْتَجُّ اللَّهُ: Allah establishes the proof or argument against His creation

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the divine creation and recognition of the Imam?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the divinely ordered creation and designation of the Imam, portraying his origin, early perception, and heavenly marking as signs of his special status. It also states that after the passing of the preceding Imam, the succeeding Imam is granted a light by which he perceives the deeds of creation, through which Allah establishes His proof over the people.
